title: The Compromised Workstation
briefing: A workstation used by a researcher at Northbridge Fictional Corp showed unusual system behavior after opening a suspicious archive. Inspect the simulated file metadata, running processes, startup entries, and network connections to separate real indicators from routine activity.
learning_objectives: Examine simulated process lists, file metadata, startup entries, and network connections for malware indicators
Distinguish suspicious workstation activity from normal operating system and productivity tasks
Select an appropriate containment response and explain the reasoning

evidence.title: Workstation Process & Startup Snapshot
evidence.content:
PID 1420 | updater_helper.exe | path=C:\Users\m.alvarez\AppData\Local\Temp\updater_helper.exe | parent=explorer.exe | startup_entry=HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\UpdaterHelper
PID 2884 | outbound_conn=203.0.113.77:8443 | protocol=TCP | status=ESTABLISHED

evidence.title: Dropped Script Metadata
evidence.content:
File: C:\Users\m.alvarez\AppData\Local\Temp\updater_helper.exe
Signer: Unsigned (simulated indicator)
Created: 2026-11-21 09:14:02 UTC
Observed Behavior: Writes temporary report bundle and initiates connection to 203.0.113.77:8443

evidence.title: Routine Office & System Activity
evidence.content:
PID 912 | notes_editor.exe | path=C:\Program Files\NorthbridgeNotes\notes_editor.exe | status=RUNNING
PID 1044 | local_sync_agent.exe | destination=10.20.2.10:443 | status=IDLE

decisions.prompt: After identifying an unsigned helper binary in a temporary folder with a startup entry and an outbound connection to 203.0.113.77:8443, what is the best immediate response?
options: Leave the workstation online so the suspicious process keeps running
Isolate the workstation from the network, preserve evidence, and escalate to incident response/IT
Rename the suspicious file inside the Temp folder without notifying anyone
decisions.feedback_correct: Isolating the host from the network while preserving evidence helps contain potential malware activity and stops further outbound communication.
decisions.feedback_incorrect: Leaving a potentially infected host connected or making ad-hoc file changes without containment can allow further spread or complicate investigation.

hints.text: Start by checking where executable files are running from and whether any new startup entries or outbound connections stand out.
Compare the Temp folder process/connection and file metadata against normal office and local sync activity.
Look closely at updater_helper.exe in AppData\Local\Temp, its Run key entry, and the connection to 203.0.113.77:8443.
Malware indicators on a host often include unexpected executables in temporary paths, persistence via startup entries, and unusual external connections.

conclusion.prompt: Summarize the workstation indicators you found, why they are concerning, and what containment action you recommend.
